proposed_from.topic: Least-favourable face-multiplier inference for sharp survivor-complier benefit bounds. Fix finite covariate support J>=2 and ordered outcome support K>=3 in the conditional-IV model with consistency, exclusion, no defiers, weak cellwise selection monotonicity, fixed covariate and instrument-overlap lower bounds, aggregate survivor-complier mass bounded away from zero, and a nonredundant raw-capacity covariance eigenvalue band; impose no lower bound on individual cell survivor masses, no sign margin on the survivor-mass gap, and no Ferrers-cut separation. Starting from the banked exact selected-complier partial-transport capacities and closed sharp benefit endpoints, use the unscreened nonnegative-projection plug-in and define the least-favourable survivor-support face envelope by retaining every capacity, zero-gap, survivor-minimum, lower-cut, upper-cut, and mass-cap branch within a_n, where a_n tends to zero and sqrt(n)a_n tends to infinity. Prove that the conditional multiplier quantile of the finite retained-gradient maximum gives uniform root-n coverage of the entire sharp identified interval over triangular arrays with simultaneous ties and changing survivor support, without deterministic padding; prove oracle face-envelope equivalence on separated faces; and prove strict asymptotic undercoverage of calibration that keeps only the empirical maximizing/minimizing branches and empirically positive survivor cells on the specified two-covariate, three-outcome contiguous witness. Computation must use the explicit finite min-cut branch gradients and no latent LP. Consumer: the Chen-Flores Job Corps principal-stratification wage analysis, which could report honest uncertainty for the fraction of always-employed compliers whose ordered wage improves. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: an unconditional-capacity reparameterization makes both endpoints finite piecewise linear-fractional maps; a finite pathwise secant-gradient argument dominates both signed endpoint errors by retained gradients. The legal changing-support witness keeps raw-capacity contrast covariance eigenvalues in [1/4,1], and direct Gaussian-limit diagnostics show material single-face undercoverage; checks covered the active upper mass cap, denominator derivatives, projection-release directions, screening bias, zero-gradient calibration, and generic directional-inference collisions. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: certify that the explicit Gaussian witness has rejection probability above 0.4 at nominal alpha=0.4; the derived finite branch decomposition reduces this to Gaussian polyhedral probabilities. EARLY KILL TEST: independently implement and certify a lower bound exceeding 0.4 for the conservative Gaussian rejection event at kappa=1; failure after correcting the implementation should pivot the witness claim or stop the kernel. proposed_from.novelty_justification: The exact selected-complier capacity and closed sharp-endpoint mapping is supplied by the completed \(\texttt{pid_slate_benefit_partialtransport}\) theorem and is not a new claim here. The closest published ordinal-inference paper is Gabriel, Sachs, and Jensen (2024), which supplies symbolic ordinal-benefit bounds, documents ordinary \(n\)-out-of-\(n\) bootstrap undercoverage at boundary laws, and uses a conservative \(m\)-out-of-\(n\) repair; it does not prove uniform no-padding whole-set coverage for the projected survivor-complier quotient. The closest general inference paper is Fang and Santos (2019), which supplies directional-derivative resampling at a fixed map and generic bootstrap-failure diagnostics; it does not prove finite secant domination for a drifting collection of quotient faces or whole-identified-set coverage. Dong and Heiler (2026) obtain efficient normal inference for smooth selected-complier mean bounds, but their trimming regularity and relevant-support overlap exclude ordered atoms and cell survivor masses converging to zero. The strict delta is the common-multiplier finite-face theorem conditional on the imported exact mapping; the atom-table experiment only verifies that the main class genuinely contains simultaneous ties and changing support with nondegenerate covariance.

seed_details.anchor_location_read: Introduction, Theorems 1--3 and their finite response-function construction, and Section 6 Discussion, especially the stated boundary-inference problem.
seed_details.opportunity: Derive a finite secant-gradient envelope for both sharp survivor-complier benefit endpoints and use a common multiplier maximum for uniform whole-set coverage through simultaneous cut, projection, and support ties.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace resampling of the selected symbolic endpoint by an unconditional-capacity reparameterization and a pathwise finite-piece secant majorization before Gaussian calibration.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for survivor-complier probability-of-benefit inference combined with face retention found ordinal bounds and selected-complier mean-bound inference in separate papers, but no theorem for the projected quotient map.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from Fang and Santos because the endpoints are merely directionally differentiable finite maxima.
seed_details.rebuttal: Fang and Santos estimate a directional derivative at a fixed law; they do not provide the signed secant domination, changing projection support, common random denominator, or whole-identified-interval uniformity required here.

seed_details.anchor_location_read: Introduction, Theorems 3.1--3.2 and the bootstrap-failure construction, and Section 5 Conclusion.
seed_details.opportunity: Construct a legal two-covariate, three-outcome contiguous survivor-support experiment and certify strict undercoverage of empirical-single-face calibration by Gaussian polyhedral probability bounds.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: After the generic nonlinearity diagnostic, impose the exact IV and selection restrictions and reduce rejection to finitely many affine Gaussian regions with the denominator and projection-release directions retained.
seed_details.destination_search: The destination search found generic inconsistency results and simulation evidence, but no legal survivor-complier distribution with an explicit covariance band and a certified numerical rejection gap.
seed_details.red_team: The witness is a hand-tuned max-of-two Gaussian toy already covered by generic bootstrap-failure theory.
seed_details.rebuttal: The witness embeds vanishing survivor support, an active mass cap, projection release, two endpoint signs, and a nondegenerate twelve-dimensional raw-capacity covariance; the remaining certificate is explicitly exposed rather than replaced by the toy max calculation.

seed_details.anchor_location_read: Introduction, Sections 2--3's recommended generalized-moment-selection statistic and critical value, the automatic tuning construction, and the concluding finite-sample comparison.
seed_details.opportunity: Characterize when the near-face procedure equals an oracle that knows the survivor support and every population active branch.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace normalized moment slack by joint slack for projection coordinates, survivor minima, zero gaps, ordered cuts, and mass caps, then prove exact retained-family recovery.
seed_details.destination_search: Moment-selection and optimized-value searches found slack screening and localized argmax sets but no simultaneous support-and-cut selection lemma for a projected ratio.
seed_details.red_team: This is a routine finite-union consistency lemma once all branch gaps are separated.
seed_details.rebuttal: The result is retained only as a sharpening theorem, not the kernel; its nontrivial content is simultaneous recovery of denominator, projection-release, and nested min-cut faces.

seed_details.anchor_location_read: Introduction, Proposition 3.1, Section 4.4 Assumptions A.1--A.7, Theorem 4.1, and its influence-function proof in Appendix C.3.
seed_details.opportunity: Build jointly orthogonal scores for every ordinal transport capacity and couple cross-fitting to near-active-face inference with flexible covariates.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the donor paper's smooth trimmed-mean bound score by a vector score for all ordered-outcome cut capacities before applying the nonsmooth endpoint map.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches pairing orthogonal selected-complier inference with ordinal probability-of-benefit bounds found Dong and Heiler and Gabriel, Sachs, and Jensen separately, with no combined theorem.
seed_details.red_team: This is a routine DML wrapper around finitely many cell probabilities.
seed_details.rebuttal: With continuous covariates the survivor direction, support, and active cut drift over covariate regions, so finite-cell localization no longer applies and the empirical-process step is genuinely different.

seed_details.anchor_location_read: Section 4.4's strong-overlap discussion, Theorem 4.1, and the Appendix C.3 linearization by the always-selected-complier denominator.
seed_details.opportunity: Let aggregate survivor-complier mass decay and derive the attainable estimation rate and non-Gaussian transition for sharp benefit endpoints, with a matching local lower bound.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Retain the random denominator rather than bounding it away from zero and analyze the ratio experiment under a mass sequence \(M_n\downarrow0\).
seed_details.destination_search: The weak-identification search found irregular propensity and weak-instrument analogies but no minimax rate frontier for survivor-complier ordinal coupling bounds.
seed_details.red_team: The rate is the immediate delta-method rate \((nM_n^2)^{-1/2}\).
seed_details.rebuttal: Projection and changing active cuts can dominate the quotient rate, and a valid seed would require a matching experiment-level lower bound; this is not assumed here.

seed_details.anchor_location_read: Proposition 4.1, Theorem 4.1, and Appendix C.3's Riesz-representer efficiency argument.
seed_details.opportunity: Derive the semiparametric efficiency bound for each survivor-benefit endpoint on separated smooth faces and construct an attaining estimator.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the trimmed-mean numerator influence function by the explicit active-cut transport-capacity numerator and propagate the shared denominator derivative.
seed_details.destination_search: No paper located an efficiency bound for the same-unit survivor-complier probability of ordinal improvement; adjacent results cover mean effects or full-arm ordinal bounds.
seed_details.red_team: Once the active face is separated, the efficient influence function is an automatic chain rule.
seed_details.rebuttal: The objection substantially holds, so this candidate is not used as a kernel; its smooth reduction is retained only as a sanity check for the uniform method.

seed_details.anchor_location_read: Introduction, Theorem 1 and its orthogonal-score proof, the multiple-outcome support-function construction, and the Conclusion.
seed_details.opportunity: Choose a constrained Job Corps targeting rule by maximizing a lower bound on the fraction of always-employed compliers who benefit, and derive regret to the robust oracle.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace estimation of a fixed support function by empirical maximization over a policy class whose score is a sharp survivor-benefit lower endpoint.
seed_details.destination_search: Policy-learning searches located robust welfare maximization for partially identified means, but no result for the ratio of ordinal partial-transport capacities among survivor compliers.
seed_details.red_team: The binary Job Corps instrument supplies no policy menu, so the policy object is imported rather than demanded by the application.
seed_details.rebuttal: The objection holds for the present data structure; a multi-program or eligibility-rule design would be needed, so this seed is dropped rather than padded.

seed_details.anchor_location_read: Introduction, Propositions 1--2 and their principal-stratum mixture construction, and Section 4 Conclusion.
seed_details.opportunity: Invert the known Job Corps assignment randomization to obtain a finite-sample confidence set for a finite-population survivor-complier benefit bound.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace superpopulation multinomial approximation by a sharp-null completion and assignment-orbit inversion over compatible principal strata.
seed_details.destination_search: Randomization and conformal searches found inversion for sharp causal nulls, but not a tractable symmetry orbit for a partially identified same-unit benefit query with latent compliance and selection strata.
seed_details.red_team: The benefit query is not sharp under the assignment orbit, so enumeration requires the same latent completion problem and yields no usable pivotal score.
seed_details.rebuttal: The obstruction is decisive in the present model; the M17 lane has no credible survivor and is dropped.

seed_details.anchor_location_read: Section 6 Discussion on boundary-sensitive confidence intervals, together with the symbolic finite-bound construction in Section 3.
seed_details.opportunity: Derive a data-driven subsample size whose endpoint law is first-order equivalent to the least-favourable face envelope over a quantified tie-separation frontier.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Express the subsampling drift and face-retention tolerance on the same local slack scale and solve for the boundary at which their critical values agree.
seed_details.destination_search: The search found generic \(m\)-out-of-\(n\) repairs and moment-selection procedures, but no observable equivalence frontier for these benefit endpoints.
seed_details.red_team: Any claimed frontier depends on an unobservable local branch gap and is therefore only a relabelling of tuning choices.
seed_details.rebuttal: No observed-data primitive frontier was obtained in the deep scan, so the candidate is dropped under the M2 requirement.
